title: Protocol for Generation and Regeneration of PEG-Passivated Slides for Single-Molecule Measurements
author: Paul, Myong
materials: This method describes the single-molecule pull-down experiments where 0.1% SDS is used to regenerate the surface bound antibody. Generally, in pull-down assay, biotinylated antibodies against the protein-of-interest are immobilized on a passivated microscope slide. The surface-tethered antibody captures the partner protein through physiological interaction (Jain et al., 2011). Then, applied non-biotinylated fluorophore label DNA/RNA interact with immobilized protein and the fluorescence signal is detected through TIRF microscopy.9.Regeneration of antibody using 0.1% SDS.a.Follow steps from 5a-d.b.Flow 50 μL of 10 nM biotin conjugated antibody either in T50 or experimental buffer.Note: In pull down experiments, the exact antibody used is dependent on the tag attached on the corresponding protein-of-interest. For instance, biotinylated anti-GFP antibodies (Rockland Antibodies & Assays, Cat#600406215) are used for GFP-tagged protein, and anti-His antibodies (Qiagen, Cat#34660) are used for His-tagged proteins. The antibody dilution (∼10 nM) needs to be optimized for each protein-antibody pair (generally in the range of 100× to 2000× dilution). (Troubleshooting 5)c.Incubate for 3–5 min.d.Wash with 50 μL T50 or experimental buffer.e.Flow 50 μL 10 nM tagged protein (corresponding to the surface-tethered antibody) in T50 or experimental buffer.f.Incubate for ∼10 min.g.Wash with 50 μL T50 or experimental buffer.Note: Make sure no air bubbles pass through the channel during the entire pull-down experiment.h.Flow 50 μL of 10 nM non-biotinylated DNA or RNA construct that can bind with surface-tethered protein. (Troubleshooting 3)i.Incubate for ∼10 min.j.Wash with 50 μL of T50 or experimental buffer.k.Flow 50 μL of imaging buffer.l.Turn on the excitation laser for recording movies. The microscope stage needs to be adjusted for proper focusing of the single-molecule surface.Note: The DNA or RNA density on the single-molecule surface needs to be optimized approximately 300–400 molecules per field of view.m.Record 20 short movies (2 s) at different imaging areas with the donor excitation laser for making the FRET histogram, if applicable. A shutter manager can be used to excite the donor and acceptor dyes.n.Record 3–4 long movies (120 s) at different imaging areas with the donor excitation laser to visualize individual molecules.o.Flow 50 μL of 0.1% SDS with T50 or experimental buffer.p.Incubate for ∼1 min.q.Wash 2–3 times with 50 μL of T50 or experimental buffer.r.Follow steps 9h-n to perform additional experimental conditions. This is one round of regeneration.Note: Treatment with 0.1% SDS is usually not harsh enough to disrupt the antibody interactions of surface-bound protein, but it is sufficient to release the bound DNA or RNA. If 0.1% SDS is sufficient to disrupt the antibody-protein interaction, repeat steps 9e-n to flow the protein-of-interest again.s.Follow steps 9o-r for another round of regeneration and repeat for multiple rounds of regeneration as needed.Note: Use the 7M NaOH treatment to change one biotinylated antibody to another biotinylated antibody following the steps described in Method 3.

steps.title: Initial slide cleaning
steps.instruction: Clean 3 × 1 in, 1 mm thick slides (used or new) before surface functionalization.

substeps.instruction: For used slides, soak ~5 h in ethanol or acetone.
Boil in water and sonicate in 5 % (w/v) Alconox detergent for 5–10 min (Branson ultrasonic bath).
Wash with tap water and gently scrub with a gloved finger.
Rinse with Milli‑Q water and place slides in a holder jar filled with Milli‑Q water.
For new slides, drill 5–6 pairs of holes side‑by‑side with a diamond needle, wash, scrub, and store in a water‑filled jar.
Burn both sides of each slide with a propane torch (using forceps), cool with N₂ gas, and store in a dry holder jar.
Scrub coverslips with a gloved finger, place 2–3 extra coverslips in a water‑filled jar; handle all glass with clean forceps.

steps.title: KOH treatment of slides
steps.instruction: Introduce surface hydroxyl groups by treating slides and coverslips with 1 M KOH.

substeps.instruction: Equilibrate aminosilane (stored at –20 °C) at ~25 °C for ≥1 h before use.
Fill slide and coverslip jars with 1 M KOH.
Sonicate jars for 30–45 min (Branson ultrasonic bath).
Discard KOH, rinse jars with Milli‑Q water, refill with Milli‑Q water.
Sonicate again for 20–30 min, then rinse with Milli‑Q water.
Burn slides to dry, cool with N₂ gas, and place in a dry jar.
Dry coverslips with N₂ gas, quickly flame‑pass 5–6 times, then place in a dry jar.
Rinse both jars with methanol, dry completely, and keep slides and coverslips in separate dry jars (avoid water to prevent aminosilane hydrolysis).

steps.title: Amino-silanization of slides
steps.instruction: Covalently attach aminosilane to the hydroxyl‑terminated glass surfaces.

substeps.instruction: Add 150 mL methanol to a clean, dry 500 mL flask.
Add 2 mL glacial acetic acid and 2 mL N‑(2‑Aminoethyl)‑3‑Aminopropyltrimethoxysilane; swirl to mix.
Immediately pour the solution into the slide and coverslip jars until full.
Incubate in the dark for 10 min, sonicate 1 min, then incubate another 30 min in the dark.

steps.title: PEGylation of slides
steps.instruction: Attach methoxy‑PEG and biotin‑PEG to the aminosilane‑treated surfaces to create a passivated, biotinylated layer.

substeps.instruction: Prepare fresh 100 mM bicarbonate buffer (84 mg NaHCO₃ in 10 mL water).
Rinse slides and coverslips with a generous amount of Milli‑Q water and dry with N₂ gas (handle coverslips gently to avoid breakage).
Weigh 180–190 mg mPEG‑SVA and 2–3 mg Biotin‑PEG‑SVA per 12 slides; dissolve in 900 µL bicarbonate buffer.
Mix by gentle pipetting up/down, then centrifuge at 12,000 × g for 1 min (solution should become clear).
Dispense 70 µL of the PEG solution onto each slide, immediately sandwich with a coverslip, avoiding air bubbles (use fine‑tip forceps).
Incubate in the dark for 3–5 h. (Optional: repeat the entire PEG step for a second round to improve passivation.)

steps.title: Store PEG-passivated slides
steps.instruction: Wash, dry, and archive the PEGylated slide‑coverslip pairs for future use.

substeps.instruction: Wash slides and coverslips again with a generous amount of Milli‑Q water.
Dry with N₂ gas.
Transfer each slide‑coverslip pair to a 50 mL tube, faces away from each other.
Vacuum‑seal the tube with a food‑saver bag and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Assemble microfluidic slide
steps.instruction: Construct a flow channel by sandwiching a coverslip onto a PEGylated slide using double‑sided tape and epoxy.

substeps.instruction: Remove stored slide tube from –20 °C, equilibrate at ~25 °C for 15–20 min.
Tear a 5–7 cm piece of 0.1 mm thick Scotch double‑sided tape; cut into ~1 mm strips with a clean razor blade.
Place the PEGylated slide (PEG side up) on a clean surface, then place the PEGylated coverslip (PEG side up) on top of the tape strip.
Lift the tape strip with a razor blade and gently lay it between each drilled hole on the slide surface.
Press the coverslip onto the taped slide using a 200‑µL (or 1000‑µL) pipet tip or the blunt edge of a razor blade.
Seal the four edges of the slide‑coverslip sandwich with quick‑drying epoxy applied with a 10‑µL pipet tip; avoid excess epoxy that could block holes.
Allow epoxy to dry for 5–10 min.

steps.title: Create flow reservoirs
steps.instruction: Add buffer reservoirs and syringe‑attachment molds to the assembled slide for automated flow.

substeps.instruction: Cut the upper part of 200 µL pipet tips to make small reservoir pieces.
Attach these reservoir pieces around each drilled hole at the top of the slide using epoxy.
Insert 10 µL pipet tips into the remaining drilled holes and seal with epoxy to form syringe‑attachment molds.
Let epoxy cure for 15–20 min, then carefully remove the 10 µL tips.
Cut the 10 µL tip, epoxy‑glue a 2 mm tube inside the cut tip, and connect the tube to a 1 mL syringe with a Luer‑lock needle.

steps.title: Regenerate surface with 0.1% SDS
steps.instruction: Repeatedly remove DNA/RNA‑bound protein from a PEG‑biotin slide using 0.1 % SDS while recording single‑molecule data.

substeps.instruction: Place the assembled slide on the TIRF microscope (after instrument calibration).
Flow 50 µL NeutrAvidin (100 µg/mL) in T50 or experimental buffer; incubate 1–2 min; wash with 50 µL T50/experimental buffer.
Flow 50 µL of 20 pM biotinylated FRET‑labeled DNA or RNA; incubate 1–2 min; wash with 50 µL experimental buffer.
Flow 50 µL imaging buffer and turn on the laser; adjust focus.
Record 20 short (2 s) movies at different fields for FRET histogram; then record 3–4 long (120 s) movies for single‑molecule behavior.
Flow 50 µL of protein‑of‑interest at the desired concentration (use syringe pump if reservoir present; add at 10 s mark, flow rate ~1 mL/min; withdraw slightly less than added).
Record movies before and after washing free protein (wash with 50 µL T50/experimental buffer).
Flow 50 µL of 0.1 % SDS in T50 or experimental buffer (maintain salt: 100 mM NaCl or 1–5 mM MgCl₂; avoid KCl). Use freshly prepared SDS.
Incubate 1 min, then wash 2–3 times with 50 µL T50/experimental buffer.
Flow 50 µL imaging buffer and repeat the imaging steps (as above) – this completes one regeneration cycle.
Repeat the SDS wash (steps above) for a second regeneration round; continue for up to ~10 cycles as needed.
Proceed to data processing and analysis after each round.

steps.title: Helicase‑induced duplex regeneration
steps.instruction: Use a helicase to unwind surface‑tethered duplex DNA/RNA and re‑anneal a new complementary strand.

substeps.instruction: Immobilize the FRET‑labeled DNA/RNA construct as described in steps 5a‑k (NeutrAvidin, DNA binding, imaging).
Flow 50 µL imaging buffer containing the helicase of interest at the desired concentration; record movies until unwinding is complete (biotinylated strand remains bound).
Flow 50 µL of 5 nM complementary ssDNA (or ssRNA) in buffer containing 5 mM MgCl₂; incubate 5 min.
Wash 2–3 times with 50 µL experimental buffer.
Flow 50 µL imaging buffer and record movies.
Repeat helicase addition (steps b‑c) as many times as desired.

steps.title: NaOH‑induced duplex regeneration
steps.instruction: Denature surface‑tethered duplexes with 50 mM NaOH and re‑anneal a new complementary strand.

substeps.instruction: Immobilize the DNA/RNA construct and record movies as in steps 5a‑k.
Flow 50 µL of 50 mM NaOH; incubate 1 min.
Wash 2–3 times with 50 µL T50 or experimental buffer (leaves biotinylated ss strand on surface).
Flow 50 µL of 5 nM complementary ssDNA (or ssRNA) in buffer with 5 mM MgCl₂; incubate 5 min.
Wash 2–3 times with 50 µL buffer, flow 50 µL imaging buffer, and record movies.
Repeat steps b‑h if further regeneration cycles are needed.

steps.title: Regenerate PEG‑biotin surface with 7 M NaOH
steps.instruction: Strip NeutrAvidin from the PEG‑biotin surface using 7 M NaOH to reuse the slide for different experiments.

substeps.instruction: Immobilize DNA/RNA construct and record movies as in steps 5a‑k.
Flow 50 µL of 7 M NaOH; incubate 2–3 min.
Wash 2–3 times with 50 µL T50 or experimental buffer.
Re‑immobilize new DNA/RNA (steps 5b‑t) or continue regeneration with 0.1 % SDS if desired.

steps.title: Antibody regeneration using 0.1% SDS
steps.instruction: Perform pull‑down experiments and regenerate surface‑bound antibodies with 0.1 % SDS.

substeps.instruction: Immobilize DNA/RNA as in steps 5a‑d (NeutrAvidin, biotinylated construct).
Flow 50 µL of 10 nM biotin‑conjugated antibody (in T50 or experimental buffer); incubate 3–5 min; wash with 50 µL T50/experimental buffer.
Flow 50 µL of 10 nM tagged protein (matching the surface‑tethered antibody) in T50/experimental buffer; incubate ~10 min; wash with 50 µL T50/experimental buffer (avoid air bubbles).
Flow 50 µL of 10 nM non‑biotinylated DNA/RNA that binds the surface‑bound protein; incubate ~10 min; wash with 50 µL T50/experimental buffer.
Flow 50 µL imaging buffer, turn on the excitation laser, adjust focus, and record:
– 20 short (2 s) movies for FRET histogram (if applicable).
– 3–4 long (120 s) movies for single‑molecule visualization.
Flow 50 µL of 0.1 % SDS in T50/experimental buffer; incubate 1 min.
Wash 2–3 times with 50 µL T50/experimental buffer.
Repeat imaging steps (as above) for additional experimental conditions; this completes one regeneration round.
If 0.1 % SDS does not disrupt antibody‑protein interaction, repeat steps e‑n to flow protein again.
For further rounds, repeat the SDS wash (steps o‑q) as many times as needed; optionally use 7 M NaOH (Method 3) to replace one biotinylated antibody with another.

steps.title: Analyze single‑molecule data
steps.instruction: Process recorded movies to generate histograms and trace analyses.

substeps.instruction: Map individual molecules using instrument calibration data.
Process movies with the standard IDL mapping file (see data and code availability).
Build FRET histograms and analyze single‑molecule traces using the provided MATLAB scripts.
Perform statistical comparisons (e.g., unpaired t‑test) across regeneration rounds as needed.

description: This protocol describes how to generate the PEG-passivation on slides and reuse the same PEG-passivated channel in single-molecule measurements, especially in the context of DNA or RNA binding proteins and antibody regeneration during pull-down experiments. The workflow described in this protocol takes a few hours in addition to the time needed for surface passivation and preparation of buffer, samples, and calibration of the instrument (see materials and equipment). It is advisable that you perform the following steps: First, prepare the required DNA or RNA and purify the protein-of-interest. Usually biotinylated and/or fluorescently labeled DNA or RNA molecules (from Integrated DNA Technologies) are tethered on the surface for single-molecule measurements. An untagged protein may be used when RNA or DNA are tethered to the surface. Second, a tagged protein is required for antibody immobilization to the single-molecule surface during pull-down experiment. Third, the total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) microscopy should be properly calibrated using a standard sample. Follow the safety protection protocol for lasers as per the institution’s recommendations.
